query_text: As a pirate captain, what would you say to your crew to motivate them to search for hidden treasure?

parts.text:
*(Slams a heavy, dust-covered leather map onto the wooden table, the ring of gold coins echoing in the quiet of the captain’s quarters before stepping out onto the deck to face the crew.)*

"Gather ’round, ye beautiful, gold-hungry scoundrels! Bring your ears to the mast and listen close! 

Look at yourselves. Are we honest merchants, sweating away our lives for a pittance of copper under the thumb of some fat, powdered governor? *No!* We are the lords of the tide! We are the free souls who look at the horizon and say, 'That belongs to us!'

But lately, our pockets have been lighter than a ghost’s whisper, and our throats drier than a desert isle. I see you looking at your empty tankards. I see you patching your boots with scrap sailcloth. Well, I say **no more!**

*(He taps the ancient parchment resting on the barrel)*

Do you see this? This isn’t just ink and sheepskin. This is the key to a kingdom. This is the chart to the Obsidian Hoard. 

The legends say it’s cursed. They say the island is guarded by the shrieking ghosts of those who died trying to claim it. They say the reef will tear the hull from any ship that dares to draw near. But I look out at this deck, and I don't see men who scare at bedtime stories. I see the fiercest, most ruthless, black-hearted crew to ever fly the Jolly Roger! If a ghost wants to keep my gold, he’ll have to fight me for it twice!

Think of what waits for us under those sands, lads. Chests of Spanish doubloons so heavy they'll make the timber groan! Rubies the size of a coxswain’s fist! Emeralds that glow greener than the sea itself! 

We find this treasure, and not a man among you will ever have to haul a rope again—unless it’s to hoist your own sails on your own damn ship! We’ll drink the finest rum from golden chalices, we'll wear silk fit for kings, and those high-born nobles who call us 'criminals' will bow to our wealth! 

We can sit here and rot in the doldrums, or we can sail into the teeth of the gale and take what is ours by right of steel and gunpowder! 

So, what say ye, ye scurvy dogs?! Will we let a few old bones and a bit of rough water stand between us and a life of absolute luxury? Or do we sail for glory, gold, and the sweet, sweet taste of freedom?!

**To the rigging, ye bastards! Hoist the black flag, weigh the anchor, and let’s go rob the devil himself!**"
